children: are expanding their collaboration to help engineers and construction teams manage increasingly complex electrical systems throughout a building’s lifecycle.

Eaton developed Workbench 360 to connect its electrical-equipment data, engineering expertise and project information with Autodesk Revit, Forma and Tandem. The system is intended to improve coordination as projects move from design through construction and into long-term operation.

Engineers using Revit will be able to access Eaton product information, building information modeling content and engineering support earlier in the design process. During construction, Workbench 360 will use Autodesk Forma Build to provide information about equipment status, submittals, order milestones, shipping and other project updates.

Once a building is operational, the connected project and equipment data can support Autodesk Tandem and Eaton’s Brightlayer digital energy twin technology. These tools can help customers monitor assets and optimize energy use.

The companies said the collaboration is designed to reduce manual data transfers and prevent important information from being lost between different stages of a project. It is aimed at commercial buildings, campuses, healthcare facilities and data centers, where electrical systems are becoming more complicated as power demand and electrification increase.
Eaton and Autodesk did not disclose financial terms or provide revenue projections for the expanded partnership.
